claims.source: Aortic valves mainly derive from endocardial cushion progenitors with a potential contribution from other cellular sources (epicardial cells and neural crest) (Wu et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Wu et al., 2017

claims.claim: Valve formation depends on cell proliferation mediated by the vegf-nfat1 pathway
claims.source: Generally, valve formation depends on two main events: cell proliferation, which is mainly mediated by the vegf-nfat1 pathway, matrix deposition and an endothelial-to-mesenchymal transformation (endMT) under the control of Gata transcription factors (Laforest et al., 2011; Stefanovic et al., 2014), Notch signaling (Luxán et al., 2016), Smad/tgf-beta/Bmp, and Wnt-beta catenin signals (Combs and Yutzey, 2009).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Laforest et al., 2011; Stefanovic et al., 2014; Luxán et al., 2016; Combs and Yutzey, 2009

claims.claim: Arterial valves develop differently from atrioventricular valves by differentiating directly from progenitors in the outflow wall independently from endMT in mouse
claims.source: Nevertheless, recent evidence suggests that arterial valves develop differently from atrioventricular valves by differentiating directly from progenitors in the outflow wall independently from endMT in mouse (Eley et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Eley et al., 2018

claims.claim: Aortic valves are located in areas of high flow velocity
claims.source: Aortic valves are located in areas of high flow velocity and mechanical forces have a great impact on valve morphogenesis (Butcher et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Butcher et al., 2008

claims.claim: Abnormal blood circulation is a cardiovascular risk factor
claims.source: Abnormal blood circulation is widely recognized as a cardiovascular risk factor and abnormal mechanotransduction has been associated with valvulopathies (Bäck et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Bäck et al., 2013

claims.claim: Congenital heart valve malformations are associated with genetic mutations in genes essential for heart valve development
claims.source: Congenital heart valve malformations are usually associated with genetic mutations in genes essential for heart valve development, such as signaling factors (Notch1, TGFβ) for the aortic valves (Bäck et al., 2013), and actin-binding proteins (FilaminA) for the mitral valves (Sauls et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Bäck et al., 2013 and Sauls et al., 2012

claims.claim: Genetic mutations linking valve defects with genes involved in controlling developmental programs have been discovered
claims.source: The reoccurring discovery of genetic mutations linking valve defects with genes involved in controlling developmental programs (e.g., in NOTCH1, TBX5, GATA4, TBX20, LMCD1, TNS1, and DCHS1) (PROMESA investigators et al., 2015; Durst et al., 2015; Garg et al., 2005; Richards and Garg, 2010), has spurred interest in valve morphogenesis.
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to PROMESA investigators et al., 2015; Durst et al., 2015; Garg et al., 2005; Richards and Garg, 2010

claims.claim: The zebrafish heart is two chambered and contains three sets of valves
claims.source: Zebrafish heart is two chambered and contains three sets of valves (the outflow tract (OFT), atrioventricular (AVC) and the inflow tract (IFT) valve [Figure 1A]) that are all bicuspid (Beis et al., 2005; Hsu et al., 2019; Tessadori et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Beis et al., 2005; Hsu et al., 2019; Tessadori et al., 2012

claims.claim: Zebrafish heart valves originate from progenitors located in the ventricle and atrium
claims.source: Zebrafish heart valves originate from progenitors located in the ventricle and atrium that generate the valve leaflets through a coordinated set of endocardial tissue movements (Boselli et al., 2017; Pestel et al., 2016; Steed et al., 2016a; Steed et al., 2016b; Vermot et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Boselli et al., 2017; Pestel et al., 2016; Steed et al., 2016a; Steed et al., 2016b; Vermot et al., 2009

claims.claim: In the zebrafish AVC, blood flow and Klf2a control notch1b and bmp4 expression, both necessary for valve formation
claims.source: In the zebrafish AVC, blood flow and Klf2a control notch1b and bmp4 expression, both of which are necessary for valve formation (Vermot et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Vermot et al., 2009

claims.claim: Klf2a regulates the deposition of matrix protein (in particular Fibronectin1) in the valve forming area
claims.source: Klf2a regulates the deposition of matrix protein (in particular Fibronectin1) in the valve forming area (Steed et al., 2016b), as well as Wnt signaling by controlling wnt9b expression (Goddard et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Steed et al., 2016b and Goddard et al., 2017

claims.claim: Canonical Wnt signals arise specifically in sub-endocardial, abluminal cells and are dependent upon hemodynamic forces in zebrafish
claims.source: The latter is consistent with the fact that canonical Wnt signals arise specifically in sub-endocardial, abluminal cells and that these Wnt signals are dependent upon hemodynamic forces in zebrafish (Pestel et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Pestel et al., 2016

claims.claim: Notch signaling is essential for aortic valve formation
claims.source: In addition, Notch signaling is essential for aortic valve formation (Garg, 2016) and OFT development (MacGrogan et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Garg, 2016; MacGrogan et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2017

claims.claim: Fluid shear stress is an important environmental cue that governs vascular physiology and pathology
claims.source: Fluid shear stress is an important environmental cue that governs vascular physiology and pathology (Baeyens et al., 2016), but the molecular mechanisms that mediate endocardial responses to flow are only partially understood.
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Baeyens et al., 2016

claims.claim: In zebrafish, the mechanosensitive channels Trpv4 and Trpp2 modulate endocardial calcium signaling and klf2a expression necessary for valve morphogenesis
claims.source: In zebrafish, the mechanosensitive channels Trpv4 and Trpp2 modulate endocardial calcium signaling and klf2a expression is necessary for valve morphogenesis and downstream pathway activation (Heckel et al., 2015; Steed et al., 2016b).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Heckel et al., 2015 and Steed et al., 2016b

claims.claim: Notch signaling is tightly involved in cellular mechanosensitive responses in human aortic valves
claims.source: Notch signaling is tightly involved in cellular mechanosensitive responses in human aortic valves (Godby et al., 2014) and Notch1 is a potent mechanosensor in adult arteries (Mack et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Godby et al., 2014 and Mack et al., 2017

claims.claim: Stretch-sensitive channels from the Piezo family are important for vascular development
claims.source: More recently, it has been shown that stretch-sensitive channels from the Piezo family (Murthy et al., 2017) are important for vascular development (Li et al., 2014; Ranade et al., 2014) and lymphatic valve formation (Nonomura et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Murthy et al., 2017; Li et al., 2014; Ranade et al., 2014; Nonomura et al., 2018

claims.claim: Piezo channels exert essential roles during cell differentiation in the embryo
claims.source: In the embryo, Piezo channels exert essential roles during cell differentiation (He et al., 2018) and can affect lineage choice by modulating the nuclear localization of the mechanoreactive transcription coactivator Yap (Pathak et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to He et al., 2018 and Pathak et al., 2014

claims.claim: The BA dampens the pressure wave down the arterial tree
claims.source: The BA dampens the pressure wave down the arterial tree (Braun et al., 2003b).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Braun et al., 2003b

claims.claim: The BA expresses elastic fiber genes that provide mechanical properties necessary for its physiological function
claims.source: To perform its function, the BA expresses elastic fiber genes that are thought to provide the mechanical properties necessary for its physiological function (Braun et al., 2003a; Braun et al., 2003b; Keith et al., 1977).
claims.evidence: Supported by citations to Braun et al., 2003a; Braun et al., 2003b; Keith et al., 1977

claims.claim: Elastin b contributes to the development of the BA by regulating cell fate determination of cardiac precursor cells into smooth muscle via a process involving Yap1
claims.source: The extracellular matrix (ECM) gene, elastin b, contributes to the development of the BA by regulating cell fate determination of cardiac precursor cells into smooth muscle via a process that involves the mechanotransducer Yap1 (Moriyama et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: Supported by citation to Moriyama et al., 2016

claims.claim: Blood flow in the OFT is bidirectional until functional valve leaflets emerge at 144 hpf
claims.source: Live imaging of the double transgenic line Tg(gata1:ds-red; kdrl:EGFP) to follow red blood cells and endothelial cell wall movements reveal dramatic changes in intracardiac blood flow patterns during OFT valve development: as the heart matures, blood flow in the OFT is bidirectional until functional valve leaflets emerge in the OFT at 144 hpf (Figure 1A–C).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data from live imaging and Figure 1A-C

claims.claim: The periods within the cardiac cycle in which reversing flow can be observed decrease in length until 144 hpf
claims.source: Throughout development, the periods within the cardiac cycle in which reversing flow can be observed decrease in length until 144 hpf, the stage at which we could not observe reversing flow anymore (Figure 1C).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data and Figure 1C

claims.claim: At 56 hpf, the endothelium resembles a tube, maturing into cushions by 72 hpf, into premature leaflets by 96 hpf and finally into elongated, thin leaflets by 144 hpf
claims.source: Using the Tg(fli:lifeact-EGFP; kdrl:nls-mCherry) line, which labels endothelial cells, we found that these flow profile modifications are linked to changes in OFT tissue geometry and the state of OFT maturation (Figure 1B). At 56 hpf, the endothelium resembles a tube (Figure 1B,C), maturing into cushions by 72 hpf, into premature leaflets by 96 hpf and finally into elongated, thin leaflets by 144 hpf (Figure 1B,C).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data from transgenic line imaging and Figure 1B,C

claims.claim: The endothelium folds to form the valve without multilayering
claims.source: The results suggest that the endothelium folds to form the valve without multilayering (Figure 2B,C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: Supported by photoconversion experimental data shown in Figure 2B,C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A

claims.claim: Photoconverted cells remain attached to each other and do not show signs of delamination as observed in the AVC
claims.source: Indeed, we could observe that the photoconverted cells remain attached to each other and do not show signs of delamination as observed in the AVC (Figure 2B,C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: Supported by photoconversion experimental data shown in Figure 2B,C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1B

claims.claim: At 72 hpf, cushions appear and Fn1 is observed in the cells around the endothelial cells, that are themselves surrounded at their base by myocardium in the posterior part
claims.source: At 72 hpf, cushions appear and Fn1 is observed in the cells around the endothelial cells, that are themselves surrounded at their base by myocardium in the posterior part (Figure 3A,B,C,D,E).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3A,B,C,D,E

claims.claim: Fn1 expression level increases at 96 hpf and delineates a group of cells surrounding the OFT as well as in the basal side of a few endothelial cells that form the cushions
claims.source: Fn1 expression level increases at 96 hpf and delineates a group of cells surrounding the OFT as well as in the basal side of a few endothelial cells that form the cushions (Figure 3C, arrows, E).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3C,E

claims.claim: In the developed leaflets at 120 hpf, Fn1 expression is maintained within the leaflets
claims.source: In the developed leaflets at 120 hpf, Fn1 expression is maintained within the leaflets (Figure 3D,E).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3D,E

claims.claim: Most of the cells surrounding the endothelium expressing Fn1 also express Elastin b (Elnb), a marker of smooth muscle cells
claims.source: We found that most of the cells surrounding the endothelium expressing Fn1 also express Elastin b (Elnb, Eln2 or Tropoelastin), a marker of smooth muscle cells (Grimes et al., 2006; Miao et al., 2007; Paffett-Lugassy et al., 2017) (Figure 3B', C', D').
claims.evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3B', C', D' and citations to Grimes et al., 2006; Miao et al., 2007; Paffett-Lugassy et al., 2017

claims.claim: The cells surrounding the Fn1 cells are not myocardial cells as the myocardium stops just before the BA region
claims.source: We could confirm that the cells surrounding the Fn1 cells are not myocardial cells as the myocardium stops just before the BA region (Figure 3A,E).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 3A,E

claims.claim: All cells expressing Fn1 are also DAF-FMDA-positive
claims.source: To better characterize the smooth muscle identity and their activity, we performed a DAF-FMDA assay and counterstained with Fn1 at 72 hpf, 96 hpf and 120 hpf (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A). These results suggest that all cells expressing Fn1 are also DAF-FMDA-positive (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: Supported by DAF-FMDA assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A

claims.claim: Some of the Fn1-expressing cells also express Tg(wt1a:GFP), a marker of epicardial cells
claims.source: Some of these cells also express Tg(wt1a:GFP) (asterisks in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B) a marker of epicardial cells (Peralta et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: Supported by transgenic line data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and citation to Peralta et al., 2013

claims.claim: The Klf2a reporter is specifically activated in the OFT endothelium from 72 hpf to 120 hpf
claims.source: We could observe a specific activation of the Klf2a reporter in the OFT endothelium (Figure 4A,C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1), in particular in the ventricular part of the valve (posterior) from 72 hpf to 120 hpf (Figure 4C,D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: Supported by reporter line data shown in Figure 4A,C,D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1

claims.claim: The Notch reporter Tg(tp1:dGFP) is specifically expressed in the OFT endothelium in the ventricular part of the valve from 72 hpf to 120 hpf
claims.source: Similarly, the Notch reporter Tg(tp1:dGFP) is specifically expressed in the OFT endothelium (Figure 4B,C), in the ventricular part of the valve from 72 hpf to 120 hpf (Figure 4C,D).
claims.evidence: Supported by reporter line data shown in Figure 4B,C,D

claims.claim: The transgene activation is stronger in the posterior part of the valve than the anterior part throughout valve maturation for both Klf2a and Notch reporters
claims.source: Interestingly, the spatial activation of the reporter varies within the valve forming area - the transgene activation is stronger in the posterior part of the valve than the anterior part of the valve throughout the process of valve maturation (Figure 4C,D). We made similar observations for the Notch reporter (Figure 4C,D).
claims.evidence: Supported by reporter line data shown in Figure 4C,D

claims.claim: Yap1 is localized in the heart at 72 hpf, in particular in the OFT smooth muscle cells
claims.source: We found that Yap1 is localized in the heart at 72 hpf, in particular in the OFT smooth muscle cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A,B

claims.claim: The smooth muscle cells surrounding the OFT and some OFT endothelial cells express Yap1
claims.source: To better characterize its tissue-specific expression, we used the double transgenic line Tg(fli:lifeact-EGFP; kdrl:nls-mCherry) and could show that the smooth muscle cells surrounding the OFT, but also some OFT endothelial cells express Yap1 (asterisks in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunostaining data on transgenic line shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B

claims.claim: The Yap/Wwtr1-Tead reporter was activated in the OFT endothelial cells as well as the smooth muscle cells surrounding the OFT
claims.source: To assess the activity of the Hippo pathway in the heart at 72 hpf, we made use of the Tg(4xGTIIC:d2GFP) and could see that the Yap/Wwtr1-Tead reporter was activated in the OFT endothelial cells (labelled using the kdrl:membrane-mCherry line) as well as the smooth muscle cells surrounding the OFT (labelled by the Elnb staining) (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: Supported by reporter line data shown in Figure 5A

claims.claim: A significant fraction of yap1-/- embryos displayed abnormal valves (17% at 72 hpf, 8% at 96 hpf, 17% at 120 hpf)
claims.source: When analyzed from 72 hpf until 120 hpf, a significant fraction of yap1-/- embryos displayed abnormal valves (17% at 72 hpf, 8% at 96 hpf, 17% at 120 hpf, n = 12) and an increasing fraction of yap1 embryos did not have recognizable OFT valves (58% at 120hpf, n = 12).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data from mutant analysis

claims.claim: 58% of yap1 embryos did not have recognizable OFT valves at 120 hpf
claims.source: When analyzed from 72 hpf until 120 hpf, a significant fraction of yap1-/- embryos displayed abnormal valves (17% at 72 hpf, 8% at 96 hpf, 17% at 120 hpf, n = 12) and an increasing fraction of yap1 embryos did not have recognizable OFT valves (58% at 120hpf, n = 12).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data from mutant analysis

claims.claim: Yap1 is involved during OFT valve morphogenesis
claims.source: Thus, these results suggest that yap1 is involved during OFT valve morphogenesis (Figure 5B) and that smooth muscle cell progenitors are likely to play a role in the process.
claims.evidence: Supported by mutant analysis data shown in Figure 5B

claims.claim: In the group of 'beating heart' embryos (group1), stronger GFP expression is observed in the posterior part of the valve for both Klf2a and Notch reporters at every stage analyzed
claims.source: In the group of 'beating heart' embryos (group1, Video 1), we still observe stronger GFP expression in the posterior part of the valve for both reporters at every stage analyzed (Figure 6A).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data from tnnt2a morpholino experiments shown in Figure 6A

claims.claim: In the group of embryos where the heart is beating at an abnormal slow rate (group2), no difference is observed between the anterior and posterior part of the valve for the Klf2a reporter at 72 hpf
claims.source: In the group of embryos where the heart is still beating but at an abnormal slow rate (less than 2 Hz, group2, Video 2), we observe no difference between the anterior and posterior part of the valve (p=0.99) for the Klf2a reporter at 72 hpf (Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data from tnnt2a morpholino experiments shown in Figure 6B

claims.claim: For the Notch reporter, no difference in fluorescence intensity is observed at 72 hpf in the 'slow beating heart' group
claims.source: For the Notch reporter, we observed no difference in fluorescence intensity at 72 hpf (p=0.1) (Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data from tnnt2a morpholino experiments shown in Figure 6B

claims.claim: Fn1, Elnb, and Yap1 are down-regulated in the smooth muscle cells of the 'slow beating heart' embryos
claims.source: In addition, we analyzed the localization of Fn1, Elnb and Yap1 by immunostaining in both 'beating heart' (n = 4, n = 7 and n = 7, respectively) and 'slow beating heart' (n = 6, n = 7 and n = 7 respectively) groups and could observe that Fn1, Elnb, and Yap1 are down-regulated in the smooth muscle cells of the 'slow beating heart' embryos (Figure 6D,F).
claims.evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 6D,F

claims.claim: The 'slow beating heart' group has a smaller BA
claims.source: Moreover, we assessed the BA diameter and the activity of the smooth muscle using the DAF-FMDA assay (Figure 6E). The results suggest that the 'slow beating heart' group has a smaller BA (p<0,001) and the smooth muscle are much less active (p=0,05) (Figure 6E,F).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6E,F

claims.claim: The smooth muscle are much less active in the 'slow beating heart' group
claims.source: Moreover, we assessed the BA diameter and the activity of the smooth muscle using the DAF-FMDA assay (Figure 6E). The results suggest that the 'slow beating heart' group has a smaller BA (p<0,001) and the smooth muscle are much less active (p=0,05) (Figure 6E,F).
claims.evidence: Supported by DAF-FMDA assay data shown in Figure 6E,F

claims.claim: All the tnnt2aMO-injected embryos with almost no contraction have no valve
claims.source: We next assessed valve morphology in which blood flow is altered due to slow heart contraction and selected the fish with almost no contraction (group2). All the tnnt2aMO-injected embryos have no valve (n = 9/9, p<10−6) (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: Supported by experimental data from tnnt2a morpholino experiments shown in Figure 6C

claims.claim: More than 80% of vlad tepes mutant embryos displayed abnormal OFT valves
claims.source: To confirm the role of flow in the process, we analyzed the effect of altered blood viscosity and shear stress by lowering red blood cell content in the gata1 mutants (Vlad Tepes) as previously described (Steed et al., 2016b; Vermot et al., 2009). In vlad tepes mutant embryos (n = 21, p<10−2), more than 80% of the mutants displayed abnormal OFT valves (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: Supported by mutant analysis data shown in Figure 6C and citations to Steed et al., 2016b; Vermot et al., 2009

claims.claim: Most of the klf2a-/- embryos display proper valves at 72 hpf (n = 7/12), 96 hpf (n = 6/12) and 120 hpf (n = 6/12)
claims.source: We found that most of the klf2a-/- embryos display proper valves at 72 hpf (n = 7/12), 96 hpf (n = 6/12) and 120 hpf (n = 6/12).
claims.evidence: Supported by mutant analysis data

claims.claim: 33% of the klf2a-/- embryos have abnormal 'delayed phenotype' at 72 hpf (n = 4/12), at 96 hpf (n = 4/12) and 120 hpf (n = 4/12)
claims.source: However, 33% of the klf2a-/- embryos have abnormal 'delayed phenotype' at 72 hpf (n = 4/12), at 96 hpf (n = 4/12) and 120 hpf (n = 4/12) (Figure 7A).
claims.evidence: Supported by mutant analysis data shown in Figure 7A

claims.claim: 30% of the notch1b-/- embryos have a 'delayed phenotype' at 72 hpf, 35% at 96 hpf and 45% at 120 hpf
claims.source: In addition, notch1b is also necessary for proper valve formation since 30% (n = 6/20) of the notch1b-/- embryos have a 'delayed phenotype' at 72 hpf, 35% (n = 7/20) at 96 hpf and 45% (n = 9/20) at 120 hpf (Figure 7B) while almost all control embryos have proper valves at 72 hpf (n = 6/7), 96 hpf (n = 7/7) and 120 hpf (n = 7/7) (Figure 7B).
claims.evidence: Supported by mutant analysis data shown in Figure 7B

claims.claim: In klf2a-/- embryos, notch1b expression is altered with no clear expression defining the OFT region at 48 hpf (64%) and at 72 hpf (78%)
claims.source: In controls, 85% and 91% of the embryos have notch1b expression in the OFT at 48 hpf and 72 hpf, respectively (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A–C). However, in klf2a-/- embryos, notch1b expression is altered with no clear expression defining the OFT region at 48 hpf (64%) and at 72 hpf (78%) (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A,B).
claims.evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A,B,C

claims.claim: Most of the embryos show proper klf2a expression in notch1b-/- embryos (61% at 48 hpf and 51% at 72 hpf)
claims.source: However, in the reverse experiment, most of the embryos show proper klf2a expression in notch1b -/- embryos (61% at 48 hpf and 51% at 72 hpf) (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C

claims.claim: The Notch reporter is significantly more expressed in the posterior part compared to the anterior part of the valves at 72 hpf (p<10−2), 96 hpf (p<10−2) and 120 hpf (p<10−1) in the klf2a+/+ embryos
claims.source: As for Notch reporter expression in wild-type (Figure 4C,D), the Notch reporter is significantly more expressed in the posterior part compared to the anterior part of the valves at 72 hpf (p<10−2), 96 hpf (p<10−2) and 120 hpf (p<10−1) (Figure 7C,C') in the klf2a+/+ embryos.
claims.evidence: Supported by reporter line data shown in Figure 7C,C'

claims.claim: The fluorescent intensity in the posterior part of the valve is significantly reduced in the klf2a-/- compared to klf2a+/+ at 72 hpf (p<10–1), 96 hpf (p<10−1) and 120 hpf (p<10−1)
claims.source: Interestingly, the stronger posterior expression is lost in the klf2a-/- embryos and the fluorescent intensity in the posterior part of the valve is significantly reduced in the klf2a-/- compared to klf2a+/+ at 72 hpf (p<10–1), 96 hpf (p<10−1) and 120 hpf (p<10−1) (Figure 7C,C').
claims.evidence: Supported by reporter line data shown in Figure 7C,C'

claims.claim: The expression in the posterior part of the valve in the notch1b-/- embryos compared to the notch1b+/+ control embryos is not significantly different at any time point analyzed
claims.source: In comparison, the expression in the posterior part of the valve in the notch1b-/- embryos compared to the notch1b+/+ control embryos is not significantly different at any time point analyzed (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: Supported by reporter line data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1D

claims.claim: Fn1, Elnb, and Yap1 are properly localized in controls and klf2a-/- embryos

claims.evidence: Supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1E

claims.claim: Heart function in trpp2, trpv4, piezo1, and piezo2a mutants is normal based on relative fractional shortening measurements
claims.source: First, we evaluated the relative fractional shortening (RFS) at 72hpf in the atrium and in the ventricle of each mutant and their corresponding controls (Figure 8—figure supplement 1A). claims.evidence: Supported by RFS measurement data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1A

claims.claim: The retrograde flow fraction and time windows for forward, reverse or no flow are equivalent in all mutants when compared to their respective controls
claims.source: As another readout of flow forces and heart function, we quantified the retrograde flow fraction (RFF) at 72hpf and 120hpf in these mutants and the time windows for forward, reverse or no flow. We found that they are equivalent in all mutants when compared to their respective controls (Figure 8—figure supplement 1B), confirming that heart function is not different in these mutants.
claims.evidence: Supported by RFF measurement data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1B

claims.claim: 33% of the trpv4 mutant embryos have normal valves and mainly display thick valves (67%)
claims.source: We found that 33% of the trpv4 mutant embryos (n = 7) have normal valves and mainly display thick valves (67%).
claims.evidence: Supported by mutant analysis data

claims.claim: In the trpp2 mutant embryos, only 10% have normal valves and 35% are delayed with respect to valve phenotype
claims.source: In the trpp2 mutant embryos (n = 20), a stronger phenotype is observed with only 10% of normal valves. We observed that some embryos are delayed with respect to valve phenotype, meaning that the valve forming area still displays cushions at 120 hpf instead of having leaflets (35%).
claims.evidence: Supported by mutant analysis data

claims.claim: The trpv4-/-; trpp2+/- has an intermediate phenotype with 25% of the embryos having normal valves

claims.evidence: Supported by mutant analysis data

claims.claim: The trpp2-/-; trpv4-/- embryos have a stronger phenotype, with none of the embryos showing proper OFT valve development and displaying mainly a delayed valve phenotype (45%)
claims.source: Finally, the trpp2-/-; trpv4-/- embryos (n = 11) have a stronger phenotype, with none of the embryos showing proper OFT valve development and displaying mainly a delayed valve phenotype (45%).
claims.evidence: Supported by mutant analysis data

claims.claim: The piezo1 mutant embryos show mainly a delayed valve formation (50%)
claims.source: Interestingly, the piezo1 mutant embryos (n = 14) show mainly a delayed valve formation (50%), similarly to the trpv4-/-; trpp2-/- embryos.

claims.claim: The piezo2a-/- has a less stringent phenotype with mainly normal valves (44%) but 11% do not have valves at all

claims.evidence: Supported by mutant analysis data

claims.claim: In piezo1-/-; piezo2a-/- embryos, none of the fish display proper valve development and most of them do not form any valves (36%)
claims.source: This phenotype is even more prevalent in piezo1-/-; piezo2a-/- embryos (n = 11), where none of the fish display proper valve development and most of them do not form any valves (36%).

results.result: OFT valve development in zebrafish proceeds through distinct morphological stages from 56 hpf to 144 hpf, with bidirectional blood flow gradually transitioning to unidirectional flow as valve leaflets mature.
results.evaluation: Claims C25-C27 are supported by live imaging data using transgenic lines (Tg(gata1:ds-red; kdrl:EGFP) and Tg(fli:lifeact-EGFP; kdrl:nls-mCherry)) showing temporal progression of valve morphology and flow patterns with clear visual evidence in Figures 1A-C. The experimental approach is appropriate and the observations are well-documented.

results.result: OFT valve formation occurs through endothelial folding without multilayering or delamination, representing a distinct mechanism from AVC valve development.
results.evaluation: Claims C28-C29 are supported by photoconversion experiments (Figure 2B,C and supplements) tracking individual cells over time, demonstrating folding without multilayering. Claim C88 appropriately contrasts this with AVC development. The experimental design using Tg(fli:gal4FF;UAS:kaede) is sound and the conclusions are justified by the data.

results.result: OFT valve morphogenesis involves coordinated development of endothelial and smooth muscle cell layers, with Fibronectin1 and Elastin b expression marking smooth muscle progenitors surrounding the endothelium from 72-120 hpf.
results.evaluation: Claims C30-C36 are well-supported by immunostaining data (Figure 3) showing temporal and spatial expression patterns of Fn1, Elnb, and smooth muscle markers. The DAF-FMDA assay confirms functional smooth muscle activity. Sample sizes are adequate (n=4-13 depending on marker) and the multi-marker approach strengthens the conclusions. Claim C83 appropriately summarizes these findings.

results.result: Klf2a and Notch signaling are specifically activated in the posterior (ventricular) part of the OFT valve endothelium where shear stress is expected to be highest.
results.evaluation: Claims C37-C39 are supported by reporter line data (Tg(klf2a:H2B-GFP) and Tg(tp1:dGFP)) showing spatially restricted expression patterns (Figure 4). Quantification shows statistically significant differences between anterior and posterior regions (p<0.05 at all timepoints, n=5-6). Claim C89 makes a reasonable inference about shear stress based on geometry, though direct shear stress measurements are not provided.

results.result: Yap1 is expressed in both OFT endothelial cells and smooth muscle cells, and is necessary for proper OFT valve morphogenesis.
results.evaluation: Claims C40-C42 are supported by immunostaining and reporter line data (Figure 5 and supplements) showing Yap1 localization and Hippo pathway activity. Claims C43-C45 demonstrate requirement through yap1 mutant analysis showing valve defects (17-58% abnormal depending on stage, n=12). The phenotypic analysis is appropriate though sample size is modest. Claim C85 appropriately summarizes the necessity of Yap1.

results.result: Klf2a and Notch reporter expression is flow-dependent, and mechanical forces from heart contraction are necessary for valve development and smooth muscle cell identity in the OFT.
results.evaluation: Claims C46-C53 are supported by tnnt2a morpholino experiments showing loss of spatial reporter expression patterns with reduced heart contraction (Figure 6), and vlad tepes mutant analysis showing valve defects with altered blood viscosity (>80% abnormal, n=21, p<0.01). The experimental design using graded morpholino knockdown is appropriate. Statistical significance is demonstrated for key comparisons. Claims C90-C91 appropriately conclude flow-dependence based on these experiments.

results.result: Klf2a and Notch1b are both required for proper OFT valve morphogenesis, with Klf2a acting upstream to modulate Notch expression, but Klf2a is not necessary for smooth muscle cell differentiation.
results.evaluation: Claims C54-C62 are supported by comprehensive genetic analysis using klf2a and notch1b mutants (Figure 7). Valve phenotypes are documented (33-45% delayed phenotype), epistasis is demonstrated through in situ hybridization showing altered notch1b expression in klf2a mutants (64-78% altered) but not vice versa, and reporter analysis shows reduced Notch activity in klf2a mutants (p<0.05). Sample sizes are adequate (n=4-20). Claims C92-C94 appropriately summarize the genetic relationships.

results.result: Mechanosensitive channels Trpp2, Trpv4, Piezo1, and Piezo2a are required for proper OFT valve development, with varying phenotypic severity, but do not affect overall heart function.
results.evaluation: Claims C63-C64 demonstrate normal heart function in mutants through RFS and RFF measurements (Figure 8 supplement 1). Claims C65-C71 document valve phenotypes in single and double mutants with appropriate sample sizes (n=7-21). The phenotypic characterization is thorough, showing graded severity (trpp2-/-;trpv4-/- and piezo1-/-;piezo2a-/- most severe). The conclusion that channels are required for valve development is well-supported.

results.result: Piezo1 and Trpp2 have distinct roles in OFT valve development: Piezo1 inhibits klf2a expression in endothelium and regulates smooth muscle maturation, while Trpp2 is required for klf2a activation in the posterior valve endothelium.
results.evaluation: Claims C72-C77 are supported by detailed phenotypic analysis of trpp2 and piezo1 mutants showing temporal progression of defects and differential effects on molecular markers (Figure 8). Klf2a reporter analysis shows opposite effects: increased expression in piezo1 mutants (p<0.001) vs decreased in trpp2 mutants (p<0.01), supporting distinct roles (C76-C77, C95-C96). Immunostaining shows reduced Yap1, Elnb, and Fn1 in piezo1 mutants (n=7-10/10-12 affected). Claims C82 and C86 appropriately summarize the dual roles.

results.result: Piezo1 and Trpp2 are expressed in both endothelium and smooth muscle cells of the OFT, with Trpp2 showing ubiquitous expression and Piezo1 expressed at lower levels.
results.evaluation: Claims C78-C81 are supported by RNAscope data and immunohistochemistry (Figure 8 supplement 3) showing expression patterns, and by a newly generated transgenic reporter line (Tg(piezo1:nls-Venus)) confirming Piezo1 expression in smooth muscle and endothelium. The multi-method approach (RNAscope, IHC, transgenic reporter) strengthens the conclusions about expression patterns.

results.result: Piezo modulates Yap1 localization in smooth muscle cells.
results.evaluation: Claim C87 is based on immunostaining showing reduced Yap1 expression in piezo1 mutants (C74), but the study does not directly demonstrate changes in Yap1 subcellular localization. The authors acknowledge they 'were not able to assess Yap1 subcellular localization in vivo.' The claim about 'localization' vs 'expression level' is not fully supported by the presented data, though the connection between Piezo1 and Yap1 is demonstrated.

results.result: Notch and Klf2 are key flow-dependent factors necessary for correct coordination of OFT valvulogenesis.
results.evaluation: Claim C84 is supported by the combination of reporter analysis showing flow-dependent expression (C37-C39, C46-C48, C90), genetic analysis showing requirement for valve formation (C54-C56, C92), and flow manipulation experiments (C46-C53, C90-C91). The integration of multiple experimental approaches (reporters, genetics, flow manipulation) provides strong support for this conclusion.

results.result: Background claims establishing the context of valve development, mechanotransduction, and prior knowledge about relevant genes and pathways in various model systems.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C24 and C97-C104 are background/context claims supported by appropriate citations to published literature. These establish the scientific context for the study but do not represent new findings from this manuscript. The citations appear appropriate for the claims made.
